items.title: [FDD Diary #22] Change, Confirm, Breathe
content:
Rewrote the notification handler.
Hit run. 6,260 tests. Thirty seconds.

All green.

First time I changed code without holding my breath.

Before: change code, check everything by hand, miss something, find out Monday.

After: change code, run tests, thirty seconds, done.

The fear didn't vanish.
Got a way to check it.

'Something broke?'
Run tests.
'Nothing broke.'
Keep going.

Change. Confirm. Breathe. Change again.

That loop spins now.
Without fear.

Scared? Run the tests.
Thirty seconds later, the answer's there.

That's freedom.

items.title: [FDD Diary #23] Three Things Become One
content:
New feature: QUIC drops, auto-switch to HTTP.
User doesn't notice.

Wrote the spec first.
Named the place: transport folder.
Wrote the tests: switch in 3 seconds, no data loss.

Three days. Done. Clean.

All tests passed. No other features broke.
6,260 — all green.

Landed clean inside transport.
Didn't touch notification code. Didn't touch user code.

Before? No spec. AI shoves network logic inside notifications.
Two weeks. Three blowups.

Lock down the what. SDD.
Lock down the where. DDD.
Lock down the done. TDD.

Lock them down and the AI sprints inside the rails.
Fast. Accurate. Consistent.

Don't lock them down and the AI wanders.
Fast. Convincing. Different every time.

items.title: [FDD Diary #24] Yak Shaving Built the System
content:
Didn't learn any of this from textbooks.

Builds blew up. Twenty-eight left arms.
Fix one, three more break.
Lying awake thinking 'is this even right?'

The rabbit holes created the questions.
Questions found the concepts.

SDD came from builds exploding.
DDD came from code tangling.
TDD came from Monday morning dead agents.

Every framework was born from a specific pain.
Named after the frustration that created it.

Write down what you're building first.
Name where it goes.
Set the bar for done.

Three things. That's the system.

Without them, it's luck.
With them, it's repeatable.
